comparisons.whyNotMinCount: min_count bounds how many values must be PRESENT, not whether any are ABSENT, so min_count=1 returns 147945 -- the default's answer -- on a group holding eleven numbers and one empty cell. min_count=12 does return nothing known here, and only because this group has twelve rows: it would null every smaller group too. sum(skipna=False) per group is the rule itself, and the group size does not enter it.

whatTheDefaultWouldHide.note: A default sum reports that number as the group's population. It is short by the one cell nobody recorded, and no total in the result says so.

notEstablished: That summing is right for these columns. It is right for counts and wrong for rates, and neither implementation can tell which it has been given. Fieldwork offers sum and nothing else for that reason; the protection is the absence of the other option, which no check can verify.
That nothing known is the right answer rather than the honest one. It refuses to guess; a practitioner who needs the number still has to find the missing cell.
That the three supply categories are the right strata. The both-companies group is 300,149 of 486,936 people, and what to do with it is the practitioner's judgement.
